video.title: Why You Should Start Your Swing at Contact

classification.reason: The coach provides actionable cues such as 'the swing starts at contact' and 'accelerate all the way to contact', along with a specific video-scrubbing check method.

problem.title_as_question: Why should you start your swing at contact?
problem.definition: Players often stop accelerating their hand too far before contact because they intuit a large gap between acceleration and impact, which causes premature spring release and erratic ball striking.

symptoms.description: Spraying shots and losing directional control on the ball.
Hitting the ball significantly slower and missing effortless power.
Feeling forced to actively pull and manipulate the racket face with slow-twitch muscle flexing.

causes.statement: Players mentally intuit a long delay between when hand acceleration stops and when contact happens.
The player mistimes acceleration and fails to accelerate the hand all the way to the ball, letting the wrist spring release too early.
Because the spring released before the ball arrived, the brain actively flexes and pulls the racket with slow-twitch muscles to maintain string angle.
Stored elastic energy in the wrist leaks out linearly with every extra millisecond the lag release window extends beyond 40 milliseconds.

angles.summary: Scrubbing backwards three frames on a 60 fps YouTube video displays the exact 40-millisecond release window where the racket takes over the hand.
The delay between the spring release and contact is so tiny (0.04 seconds) that it physically feels almost simultaneous.
Elena Rybakina mistimed an on-the-rise forehand by releasing the spring five frames before impact, forcing an awkward slow-twitch compensation.
Amelia's forehand improved from an inefficient 12-frame release at 120 fps to a clean, elastic 5-to-6 frame release.
Elastic wrist energy leaks out linearly for every millisecond the release window is delayed past the ideal 0.04-second duration.

solutions.summary: Check your release timing on video by opening Stats for Nerds on a 60 fps clip, finding contact, and stepping back three frames with the comma key.
solutions.external_goal: Step back three frames from contact on a 60 fps video

solutions.summary: Think 'the swing starts at contact' to intuitively eliminate perceived lag delay and keep the hand accelerating directly into impact.
Intuit the swing as accelerating all the way to contact rather than trying to consciously micromanage a 40-millisecond release window.
Continue accelerating the racket until right next to the ball before letting it snap by driving through the kinetic chain with chest press, hip rotation, and a strong base.
